primaryText.ACT:18:24: Now a certain Jew named Apollos, an Alexandrian by race, an eloquent man, came to Ephesus. He was mighty in the Scriptures.

primaryText.ACT:19:3: He said, “Into what then were you baptized?” They said, “Into John’s baptism.”
primaryText.ACT:19:4: Paul said, “John indeed baptized with the baptism of repentance, saying to the people that they should believe in the one who would come after him, that is, in Christ Jesus.”
primaryText.ACT:19:5: When they heard this, they were baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus.

primaryText.ACT:21:1: When we had departed from them and had set sail, we came with a straight course to Cos, and the next day to Rhodes, and from there to Patara.
primaryText.ACT:21:2: Having found a ship crossing over to Phoenicia, we went aboard and set sail.
primaryText.ACT:21:3: When we had come in sight of Cyprus, leaving it on the left hand, we sailed to Syria and landed at Tyre, for the ship was there to unload her cargo.
primaryText.ACT:21:4: Having found disciples, we stayed there seven days. These said to Paul through the Spirit that he should not go up to Jerusalem.
primaryText.ACT:21:5: When those days were over, we departed and went on our journey. They all, with wives and children, brought us on our way until we were out of the city. Kneeling down on the beach, we prayed.
primaryText.ACT:21:6: After saying goodbye to each other, we went on board the ship, and they returned home again.
primaryText.ACT:21:7: When we had finished the voyage from Tyre, we arrived at Ptolemais. We greeted the brothers and stayed with them one day.

evidence.quote: Providence must be acknowledged when things happen thus opportunely
we kneeled down on the shore, and prayed.

primaryText.ACT:22:1: “Brothers and fathers, listen to the defense which I now make to you.”
primaryText.ACT:22:2: When they heard that he spoke to them in the Hebrew language, they were even more quiet. He said,

evidence.quote: What respectful titles he gives even to those who thus abused him
Hear you my defence; a just and reasonable request

primaryText.ACT:23:1: Paul, looking steadfastly at the council, said, “Brothers, I have lived before God in all good conscience until today.”

evidence.quote: Though his conscience was misinformed, yet he acted according to the dictates of it.
He seems rather to speak of the time since his conversion

primaryText.ACT:23:2: The high priest, Ananias, commanded those who stood by him to strike him on the mouth.
primaryText.ACT:23:3: Then Paul said to him, “God will strike you, you whitewashed wall! Do you sit to judge me according to the law, and command me to be struck contrary to the law?”
primaryText.ACT:23:4: Those who stood by said, “Do you malign God’s high priest?”
primaryText.ACT:23:5: Paul said, “I didn’t know, brothers, that he was high priest. For it is written, ‘You shall not speak evil of a ruler of your people.’”

evidence.quote: the high priest Ananias commanded them that stood by him to smite him on the mouth.
I wist not, brethren, that he was the high priest

primaryText.ACT:23:10: When a great argument arose, the commanding officer, fearing that Paul would be torn in pieces by them, commanded the soldiers to go down and take him by force from among them and bring him into the barracks.
primaryText.ACT:23:6: But when Paul perceived that the one part were Sadducees and the other Pharisees, he cried out in the council, “Men and brothers, I am a Pharisee, a son of Pharisees. Concerning the hope and resurrection of the dead I am being judged!”
primaryText.ACT:23:7: When he had said this, an argument arose between the Pharisees and Sadducees, and the crowd was divided.
primaryText.ACT:23:8: For the Sadducees say that there is no resurrection, nor angel, nor spirit; but the Pharisees confess all of these.
primaryText.ACT:23:9: A great clamor arose, and some of the scribes of the Pharisees’ part stood up, and contended, saying, “We find no evil in this man. But if a spirit or angel has spoken to him, let’s not fight against God!”

evidence.quote: The honest policy Paul used here for his own preservation was to divide his judges

primaryText.GEN:1:1: In the beginning, God created the heavens and the earth.

evidence.quote: this world was, in the beginning of time, created by a Being of infinite wisdom and power

evidence.quote: From God's being his shepherd he infers that he shall not want anything that is good for him

evidence.quote: my conscience as quickened, illuminated, and even now under the direct operation of the Holy Ghost.

primaryText.ACT:18:1: After these things Paul departed from Athens and came to Corinth.
primaryText.ACT:18:10: for I am with you, and no one will attack you to harm you, for I have many people in this city.”
primaryText.ACT:18:11: He lived there a year and six months, teaching the word of God among them.
primaryText.ACT:18:12: But when Gallio was proconsul of Achaia, the Jews with one accord rose up against Paul and brought him before the judgment seat,
primaryText.ACT:18:13: saying, “This man persuades men to worship God contrary to the law.”
primaryText.ACT:18:14: But when Paul was about to open his mouth, Gallio said to the Jews, “If indeed it were a matter of wrong or of wicked crime, you Jews, it would be reasonable that I should bear with you;
primaryText.ACT:18:15: but if they are questions about words and names and your own law, look to it yourselves. For I don’t want to be a judge of these matters.”
primaryText.ACT:18:16: So he drove them from the judgment seat.
primaryText.ACT:18:17: Then all the Greeks seized Sosthenes, the ruler of the synagogue, and beat him before the judgment seat. Gallio didn’t care about any of these things.
primaryText.ACT:18:18: Paul, having stayed after this many more days, took his leave of the brothers, and sailed from there for Syria, together with Priscilla and Aquila. He shaved his head in Cenchreae, for he had a vow.

primaryText.ACT:19:1: While Apollos was at Corinth, Paul, having passed through the upper country, came to Ephesus and found certain disciples.
primaryText.ACT:19:10: This continued for two years, so that all those who lived in Asia heard the word of the Lord Jesus, both Jews and Greeks.
primaryText.ACT:19:11: God worked special miracles by the hands of Paul,
primaryText.ACT:19:12: so that even handkerchiefs or aprons were carried away from his body to the sick, and the diseases departed from them, and the evil spirits went out.
primaryText.ACT:19:13: But some of the itinerant Jews, exorcists, took on themselves to invoke over those who had the evil spirits the name of the Lord Jesus, saying, “We adjure you by Jesus whom Paul preaches.”
primaryText.ACT:19:14: There were seven sons of one Sceva, a Jewish chief priest, who did this.
primaryText.ACT:19:15: The evil spirit answered, “Jesus I know, and Paul I know, but who are you?”
primaryText.ACT:19:16: The man in whom the evil spirit was leaped on them, overpowered them, and prevailed against them, so that they fled out of that house naked and wounded.
primaryText.ACT:19:17: This became known to all, both Jews and Greeks, who lived at Ephesus. Fear fell on them all, and the name of the Lord Jesus was magnified.
primaryText.ACT:19:18: Many also of those who had believed came, confessing and declaring their deeds.
primaryText.ACT:19:19: Many of those who practiced magical arts brought their books together and burned them in the sight of all. They counted their price, and found it to be fifty thousand pieces of silver.
primaryText.ACT:19:2: He said to them, “Did you receive the Holy Spirit when you believed?” They said to him, “No, we haven’t even heard that there is a Holy Spirit.”
primaryText.ACT:19:20: So the word of the Lord was growing and becoming mighty.
primaryText.ACT:19:21: Now after these things had ended, Paul determined in the Spirit, when he had passed through Macedonia and Achaia, to go to Jerusalem, saying, “After I have been there, I must also see Rome.”
primaryText.ACT:19:22: Having sent into Macedonia two of those who served him, Timothy and Erastus, he himself stayed in Asia for a while.
primaryText.ACT:19:23: About that time there arose no small disturbance concerning the Way.
primaryText.ACT:19:24: For a certain man named Demetrius, a silversmith who made silver shrines of Artemis, brought no little business to the craftsmen,
primaryText.ACT:19:25: whom he gathered together with the workmen of like occupation, and said, “Sirs, you know that by this business we have our wealth.
primaryText.ACT:19:26: You see and hear that not at Ephesus alone, but almost throughout all Asia, this Paul has persuaded and turned away many people, saying that they are no gods that are made with hands.
primaryText.ACT:19:27: Not only is there danger that this our trade come into disrepute, but also that the temple of the great goddess Artemis will be counted as nothing and her majesty destroyed, whom all Asia and the world worships.”
primaryText.ACT:19:28: When they heard this they were filled with anger, and cried out, saying, “Great is Artemis of the Ephesians!”
primaryText.ACT:19:29: The whole city was filled with confusion, and they rushed with one accord into the theater, having seized Gaius and Aristarchus, men of Macedonia, Paul’s companions in travel.
primaryText.ACT:19:3: He said, “Into what then were you baptized?” They said, “Into John’s baptism.”
primaryText.ACT:19:30: When Paul wanted to enter in to the people, the disciples didn’t allow him.
primaryText.ACT:19:31: Certain also of the Asiarchs, being his friends, sent to him and begged him not to venture into the theater.
primaryText.ACT:19:32: Some therefore cried one thing, and some another, for the assembly was in confusion. Most of them didn’t know why they had come together.
primaryText.ACT:19:33: They brought Alexander out of the multitude, the Jews putting him forward. Alexander beckoned with his hand, and would have made a defense to the people.
primaryText.ACT:19:34: But when they perceived that he was a Jew, all with one voice for a time of about two hours cried out, “Great is Artemis of the Ephesians!”
primaryText.ACT:19:35: When the town clerk had quieted the multitude, he said, “You men of Ephesus, what man is there who doesn’t know that the city of the Ephesians is temple keeper of the great goddess Artemis, and of the image which fell down from Zeus?
primaryText.ACT:19:36: Seeing then that these things can’t be denied, you ought to be quiet and to do nothing rash.
primaryText.ACT:19:37: For you have brought these men here, who are neither robbers of temples nor blasphemers of your goddess.
primaryText.ACT:19:38: If therefore Demetrius and the craftsmen who are with him have a matter against anyone, the courts are open and there are proconsuls. Let them press charges against one another.
primaryText.ACT:19:39: But if you seek anything about other matters, it will be settled in the regular assembly.
primaryText.ACT:19:4: Paul said, “John indeed baptized with the baptism of repentance, saying to the people that they should believe in the one who would come after him, that is, in Christ Jesus.”
primaryText.ACT:19:40: For indeed we are in danger of being accused concerning today’s riot, there being no cause. Concerning it, we wouldn’t be able to give an account of this commotion.”
primaryText.ACT:19:41: When he had thus spoken, he dismissed the assembly.
primaryText.ACT:19:5: When they heard this, they were baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus.
primaryText.ACT:19:6: When Paul had laid his hands on them, the Holy Spirit came on them and they spoke with other languages and prophesied.
primaryText.ACT:19:7: They were about twelve men in all.
primaryText.ACT:19:8: He entered into the synagogue and spoke boldly for a period of three months, reasoning and persuading about the things concerning God’s Kingdom.
primaryText.ACT:19:9: But when some were hardened and disobedient, speaking evil of the Way before the multitude, he departed from them and separated the disciples, reasoning daily in the school of Tyrannus.

primaryText.ACT:20:1: After the uproar had ceased, Paul sent for the disciples, took leave of them, and departed to go into Macedonia.
primaryText.ACT:20:10: Paul went down and fell upon him, and embracing him said, “Don’t be troubled, for his life is in him.”
primaryText.ACT:20:11: When he had gone up, had broken bread and eaten, and had talked with them a long while, even until break of day, he departed.
primaryText.ACT:20:12: They brought the boy in alive, and were greatly comforted.
primaryText.ACT:20:13: But we, going ahead to the ship, set sail for Assos, intending to take Paul aboard there; for he had so arranged, intending himself to go by land.
primaryText.ACT:20:14: When he met us at Assos, we took him aboard and came to Mitylene.
primaryText.ACT:20:15: Sailing from there, we came the following day opposite Chios. The next day we touched at Samos and stayed at Trogyllium, and the day after we came to Miletus.
primaryText.ACT:20:16: For Paul had determined to sail past Ephesus, that he might not have to spend time in Asia; for he was hastening, if it were possible for him, to be in Jerusalem on the day of Pentecost.
primaryText.ACT:20:17: From Miletus he sent to Ephesus and called to himself the elders of the assembly.
primaryText.ACT:20:18: When they had come to him, he said to them, “You yourselves know, from the first day that I set foot in Asia, how I was with you all the time,
primaryText.ACT:20:19: serving the Lord with all humility, with many tears, and with trials which happened to me by the plots of the Jews;
primaryText.ACT:20:2: When he had gone through those parts and had encouraged them with many words, he came into Greece.
primaryText.ACT:20:20: how I didn’t shrink from declaring to you anything that was profitable, teaching you publicly and from house to house,
primaryText.ACT:20:21: testifying both to Jews and to Greeks repentance toward God and faith toward our Lord Jesus.
primaryText.ACT:20:22: Now, behold, I go bound by the Spirit to Jerusalem, not knowing what will happen to me there;
primaryText.ACT:20:23: except that the Holy Spirit testifies in every city, saying that bonds and afflictions wait for me.
primaryText.ACT:20:24: But these things don’t count; nor do I hold my life dear to myself, so that I may finish my race with joy, and the ministry which I received from the Lord Jesus, to fully testify to the Good News of the grace of God.
primaryText.ACT:20:25: “Now, behold, I know that you all, among whom I went about preaching God’s Kingdom, will see my face no more.
primaryText.ACT:20:26: Therefore I testify to you today that I am clean from the blood of all men,
primaryText.ACT:20:27: for I didn’t shrink from declaring to you the whole counsel of God.
primaryText.ACT:20:28: Take heed, therefore, to yourselves and to all the flock, in which the Holy Spirit has made you overseers, to shepherd the assembly of the Lord and God which he purchased with his own blood.
primaryText.ACT:20:29: For I know that after my departure, vicious wolves will enter in among you, not sparing the flock.
primaryText.ACT:20:3: When he had spent three months there, and a plot was made against him by Jews as he was about to set sail for Syria, he determined to return through Macedonia.
primaryText.ACT:20:30: Men will arise from among your own selves, speaking perverse things, to draw away the disciples after them.
primaryText.ACT:20:31: Therefore watch, remembering that for a period of three years I didn’t cease to admonish everyone night and day with tears.
primaryText.ACT:20:32: Now, brothers, I entrust you to God and to the word of his grace, which is able to build up and to give you the inheritance among all those who are sanctified.
primaryText.ACT:20:33: I coveted no one’s silver, gold, or clothing.
primaryText.ACT:20:34: You yourselves know that these hands served my necessities, and those who were with me.
primaryText.ACT:20:35: In all things I gave you an example, that so laboring you ought to help the weak, and to remember the words of the Lord Jesus, that he himself said, ‘It is more blessed to give than to receive.’ ”
primaryText.ACT:20:36: When he had spoken these things, he knelt down and prayed with them all.
primaryText.ACT:20:37: They all wept freely, and fell on Paul’s neck and kissed him,
primaryText.ACT:20:38: sorrowing most of all because of the word which he had spoken, that they should see his face no more. Then they accompanied him to the ship.
primaryText.ACT:20:4: These accompanied him as far as Asia: Sopater of Beroea, Aristarchus and Secundus of the Thessalonians, Gaius of Derbe, Timothy, and Tychicus and Trophimus of Asia.
primaryText.ACT:20:5: But these had gone ahead, and were waiting for us at Troas.
primaryText.ACT:20:6: We sailed away from Philippi after the days of Unleavened Bread, and came to them at Troas in five days, where we stayed seven days.
primaryText.ACT:20:7: On the first day of the week, when the disciples were gathered together to break bread, Paul talked with them, intending to depart on the next day; and continued his speech until midnight.
primaryText.ACT:20:8: There were many lights in the upper room where we were gathered together.
primaryText.ACT:20:9: A certain young man named Eutychus sat in the window, weighed down with deep sleep. As Paul spoke still longer, being weighed down by his sleep, he fell down from the third floor and was taken up dead.

evidence.quote: Paul's Departure from Ephesus; Paul's Removal to Troas.
he purposed to return through Macedonia.
wolves enter in among you, not sparing the flock.

primaryText.ACT:21:1: When we had departed from them and had set sail, we came with a straight course to Cos, and the next day to Rhodes, and from there to Patara.
primaryText.ACT:21:10: As we stayed there some days, a certain prophet named Agabus came down from Judea.
primaryText.ACT:21:11: Coming to us and taking Paul’s belt, he bound his own feet and hands, and said, “The Holy Spirit says: ‘So the Jews at Jerusalem will bind the man who owns this belt, and will deliver him into the hands of the Gentiles.’”
primaryText.ACT:21:12: When we heard these things, both we and the people of that place begged him not to go up to Jerusalem.
primaryText.ACT:21:13: Then Paul answered, “What are you doing, weeping and breaking my heart? For I am ready not only to be bound, but also to die at Jerusalem for the name of the Lord Jesus.”
primaryText.ACT:21:14: When he would not be persuaded, we ceased, saying, “The Lord’s will be done.”
primaryText.ACT:21:15: After these days we took up our baggage and went up to Jerusalem.
primaryText.ACT:21:16: Some of the disciples from Caesarea also went with us, bringing one Mnason of Cyprus, an early disciple, with whom we would stay.
primaryText.ACT:21:17: When we had come to Jerusalem, the brothers received us gladly.
primaryText.ACT:21:18: The day following, Paul went in with us to James; and all the elders were present.
primaryText.ACT:21:19: When he had greeted them, he reported one by one the things which God had worked among the Gentiles through his ministry.
primaryText.ACT:21:2: Having found a ship crossing over to Phoenicia, we went aboard and set sail.
primaryText.ACT:21:20: They, when they heard it, glorified God. They said to him, “You see, brother, how many thousands there are among the Jews of those who have believed, and they are all zealous for the law.
primaryText.ACT:21:21: They have been informed about you, that you teach all the Jews who are among the Gentiles to forsake Moses, telling them not to circumcise their children and not to walk after the customs.
primaryText.ACT:21:22: What then? The assembly must certainly meet, for they will hear that you have come.
primaryText.ACT:21:23: Therefore do what we tell you. We have four men who have taken a vow.
primaryText.ACT:21:24: Take them and purify yourself with them, and pay their expenses for them, that they may shave their heads. Then all will know that there is no truth in the things that they have been informed about you, but that you yourself also walk keeping the law.
primaryText.ACT:21:25: But concerning the Gentiles who believe, we have written our decision that they should observe no such thing, except that they should keep themselves from food offered to idols, from blood, from strangled things, and from sexual immorality.”
primaryText.ACT:21:26: Then Paul took the men, and the next day purified himself and went with them into the temple, declaring the fulfillment of the days of purification, until the offering was offered for every one of them.
primaryText.ACT:21:27: When the seven days were almost completed, the Jews from Asia, when they saw him in the temple, stirred up all the multitude and laid hands on him,
primaryText.ACT:21:28: crying out, “Men of Israel, help! This is the man who teaches all men everywhere against the people, and the law, and this place. Moreover, he also brought Greeks into the temple and has defiled this holy place!”
primaryText.ACT:21:29: For they had seen Trophimus the Ephesian with him in the city, and they supposed that Paul had brought him into the temple.
primaryText.ACT:21:3: When we had come in sight of Cyprus, leaving it on the left hand, we sailed to Syria and landed at Tyre, for the ship was there to unload her cargo.
primaryText.ACT:21:30: All the city was moved and the people ran together. They seized Paul and dragged him out of the temple. Immediately the doors were shut.
primaryText.ACT:21:31: As they were trying to kill him, news came up to the commanding officer of the regiment that all Jerusalem was in an uproar.
primaryText.ACT:21:32: Immediately he took soldiers and centurions and ran down to them. They, when they saw the chief captain and the soldiers, stopped beating Paul.
primaryText.ACT:21:33: Then the commanding officer came near, arrested him, commanded him to be bound with two chains, and inquired who he was and what he had done.
primaryText.ACT:21:34: Some shouted one thing and some another, among the crowd. When he couldn’t find out the truth because of the noise, he commanded him to be brought into the barracks.
primaryText.ACT:21:35: When he came to the stairs, he was carried by the soldiers because of the violence of the crowd;
primaryText.ACT:21:36: for the multitude of the people followed after, crying out, “Away with him!”
primaryText.ACT:21:37: As Paul was about to be brought into the barracks, he asked the commanding officer, “May I speak to you?” He said, “Do you know Greek?
primaryText.ACT:21:38: Aren’t you then the Egyptian who before these days stirred up to sedition and led out into the wilderness the four thousand men of the Assassins?”
primaryText.ACT:21:39: But Paul said, “I am a Jew from Tarsus in Cilicia, a citizen of no insignificant city. I beg you, allow me to speak to the people.”
primaryText.ACT:21:4: Having found disciples, we stayed there seven days. These said to Paul through the Spirit that he should not go up to Jerusalem.
primaryText.ACT:21:40: When he had given him permission, Paul, standing on the stairs, beckoned with his hand to the people. When there was a great silence, he spoke to them in the Hebrew language, saying,
primaryText.ACT:21:5: When those days were over, we departed and went on our journey. They all, with wives and children, brought us on our way until we were out of the city. Kneeling down on the beach, we prayed.
primaryText.ACT:21:6: After saying goodbye to each other, we went on board the ship, and they returned home again.
primaryText.ACT:21:7: When we had finished the voyage from Tyre, we arrived at Ptolemais. We greeted the brothers and stayed with them one day.
primaryText.ACT:21:8: On the next day, we who were Paul’s companions departed and came to Caesarea. We entered into the house of Philip the evangelist, who was one of the seven, and stayed with him.
primaryText.ACT:21:9: Now this man had four virgin daughters who prophesied.

evidence.quote: The Prophecy of Agabus; Paul's Adherence to His Resolution to Visit Jerusalem.
whom they supposed that Paul had brought into the temple.

primaryText.ACT:22:1: “Brothers and fathers, listen to the defense which I now make to you.”
primaryText.ACT:22:10: I said, ‘What shall I do, Lord?’ The Lord said to me, ‘Arise, and go into Damascus. There you will be told about all things which are appointed for you to do.’
primaryText.ACT:22:11: When I couldn’t see for the glory of that light, being led by the hand of those who were with me, I came into Damascus.
primaryText.ACT:22:12: “One Ananias, a devout man according to the law, well reported of by all the Jews who lived in Damascus,
primaryText.ACT:22:13: came to me, and standing by me said to me, ‘Brother Saul, receive your sight!’ In that very hour I looked up at him.
primaryText.ACT:22:14: He said, ‘The God of our fathers has appointed you to know his will, and to see the Righteous One, and to hear a voice from his mouth.
primaryText.ACT:22:15: For you will be a witness for him to all men of what you have seen and heard.
primaryText.ACT:22:16: Now why do you wait? Arise, be baptized, and wash away your sins, calling on the name of the Lord.’
primaryText.ACT:22:17: “When I had returned to Jerusalem and while I prayed in the temple, I fell into a trance
primaryText.ACT:22:18: and saw him saying to me, ‘Hurry and get out of Jerusalem quickly, because they will not receive testimony concerning me from you.’
primaryText.ACT:22:19: I said, ‘Lord, they themselves know that I imprisoned and beat in every synagogue those who believed in you.
primaryText.ACT:22:2: When they heard that he spoke to them in the Hebrew language, they were even more quiet. He said,
primaryText.ACT:22:20: When the blood of Stephen, your witness, was shed, I also was standing by, consenting to his death, and guarding the cloaks of those who killed him.’
primaryText.ACT:22:21: “He said to me, ‘Depart, for I will send you out far from here to the Gentiles.’ ”
primaryText.ACT:22:22: They listened to him until he said that; then they lifted up their voice and said, “Rid the earth of this fellow, for he isn’t fit to live!”
primaryText.ACT:22:23: As they cried out, threw off their cloaks, and threw dust into the air,
primaryText.ACT:22:24: the commanding officer commanded him to be brought into the barracks, ordering him to be examined by scourging, that he might know for what crime they shouted against him like that.
primaryText.ACT:22:25: When they had tied him up with straps, Paul asked the centurion who stood by, “Is it lawful for you to scourge a man who is a Roman, and not found guilty?”
primaryText.ACT:22:26: When the centurion heard it, he went to the commanding officer and told him, “Watch what you are about to do, for this man is a Roman!”
primaryText.ACT:22:27: The commanding officer came and asked him, “Tell me, are you a Roman?” He said, “Yes.”
primaryText.ACT:22:28: The commanding officer answered, “I bought my citizenship for a great price.” Paul said, “But I was born a Roman.”
primaryText.ACT:22:29: Immediately those who were about to examine him departed from him, and the commanding officer also was afraid when he realized that he was a Roman, because he had bound him.
primaryText.ACT:22:3: “I am indeed a Jew, born in Tarsus of Cilicia, but brought up in this city at the feet of Gamaliel, instructed according to the strict tradition of the law of our fathers, being zealous for God, even as you all are today.
primaryText.ACT:22:30: But on the next day, desiring to know the truth about why he was accused by the Jews, he freed him from the bonds and commanded the chief priests and all the council to come together, and brought Paul down and set him before them.
primaryText.ACT:22:4: I persecuted this Way to the death, binding and delivering into prisons both men and women,
primaryText.ACT:22:5: as also the high priest and all the council of the elders testify, from whom also I received letters to the brothers, and traveled to Damascus to bring them also who were there to Jerusalem in bonds to be punished.
primaryText.ACT:22:6: “As I made my journey and came close to Damascus, about noon suddenly a great light shone around me from the sky.
primaryText.ACT:22:7: I fell to the ground and heard a voice saying to me, ‘Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting me?’
primaryText.ACT:22:8: I answered, ‘Who are you, Lord?’ He said to me, ‘I am Jesus of Nazareth, whom you persecute.’
primaryText.ACT:22:9: “Those who were with me indeed saw the light and were afraid, but they didn’t understand the voice of him who spoke to me.

evidence.quote: Paul's First Defence.
Ananias, a devout man according to the law

primaryText.ACT:23:1: Paul, looking steadfastly at the council, said, “Brothers, I have lived before God in all good conscience until today.”
primaryText.ACT:23:10: When a great argument arose, the commanding officer, fearing that Paul would be torn in pieces by them, commanded the soldiers to go down and take him by force from among them and bring him into the barracks.
primaryText.ACT:23:11: The following night, the Lord stood by him and said, “Cheer up, Paul, for as you have testified about me at Jerusalem, so you must testify also at Rome.”
primaryText.ACT:23:12: When it was day, some of the Jews banded together and bound themselves under a curse, saying that they would neither eat nor drink until they had killed Paul.
primaryText.ACT:23:13: There were more than forty people who had made this conspiracy.
primaryText.ACT:23:14: They came to the chief priests and the elders, and said, “We have bound ourselves under a great curse to taste nothing until we have killed Paul.
primaryText.ACT:23:15: Now therefore, you with the council inform the commanding officer that he should bring him down to you tomorrow, as though you were going to judge his case more exactly. We are ready to kill him before he comes near.”
primaryText.ACT:23:16: But Paul’s sister’s son heard they were lying in wait, and he came and entered into the barracks and told Paul.
primaryText.ACT:23:17: Paul summoned one of the centurions and said, “Bring this young man to the commanding officer, for he has something to tell him.”
primaryText.ACT:23:18: So he took him and brought him to the commanding officer and said, “Paul, the prisoner, summoned me and asked me to bring this young man to you. He has something to tell you.”
primaryText.ACT:23:19: The commanding officer took him by the hand, and going aside, asked him privately, “What is it that you have to tell me?”
primaryText.ACT:23:2: The high priest, Ananias, commanded those who stood by him to strike him on the mouth.
primaryText.ACT:23:20: He said, “The Jews have agreed to ask you to bring Paul down to the council tomorrow, as though intending to inquire somewhat more accurately concerning him.
primaryText.ACT:23:21: Therefore don’t yield to them, for more than forty men lie in wait for him, who have bound themselves under a curse to neither eat nor drink until they have killed him. Now they are ready, looking for the promise from you.”
primaryText.ACT:23:22: So the commanding officer let the young man go, charging him, “Tell no one that you have revealed these things to me.”
primaryText.ACT:23:23: He called to himself two of the centurions, and said, “Prepare two hundred soldiers to go as far as Caesarea, with seventy horsemen and two hundred men armed with spears, at the third hour of the night.”
primaryText.ACT:23:24: He asked them to provide mounts, that they might set Paul on one, and bring him safely to Felix the governor.
primaryText.ACT:23:25: He wrote a letter like this:
primaryText.ACT:23:26: “Claudius Lysias to the most excellent governor Felix: Greetings.
primaryText.ACT:23:27: “This man was seized by the Jews, and was about to be killed by them when I came with the soldiers and rescued him, having learned that he was a Roman.
primaryText.ACT:23:28: Desiring to know the cause why they accused him, I brought him down to their council.
primaryText.ACT:23:29: I found him to be accused about questions of their law, but not to be charged with anything worthy of death or of imprisonment.
primaryText.ACT:23:3: Then Paul said to him, “God will strike you, you whitewashed wall! Do you sit to judge me according to the law, and command me to be struck contrary to the law?”
primaryText.ACT:23:30: When I was told that the Jews lay in wait for the man, I sent him to you immediately, charging his accusers also to bring their accusations against him before you. Farewell.”
primaryText.ACT:23:31: So the soldiers, carrying out their orders, took Paul and brought him by night to Antipatris.
primaryText.ACT:23:32: But on the next day they left the horsemen to go with him, and returned to the barracks.
primaryText.ACT:23:33: When they came to Caesarea and delivered the letter to the governor, they also presented Paul to him.
primaryText.ACT:23:34: When the governor had read it, he asked what province he was from. When he understood that he was from Cilicia, he said,
primaryText.ACT:23:35: “I will hear you fully when your accusers also arrive.” He commanded that he be kept in Herod’s palace.
primaryText.ACT:23:4: Those who stood by said, “Do you malign God’s high priest?”
primaryText.ACT:23:5: Paul said, “I didn’t know, brothers, that he was high priest. For it is written, ‘You shall not speak evil of a ruler of your people.’”
primaryText.ACT:23:6: But when Paul perceived that the one part were Sadducees and the other Pharisees, he cried out in the council, “Men and brothers, I am a Pharisee, a son of Pharisees. Concerning the hope and resurrection of the dead I am being judged!”
primaryText.ACT:23:7: When he had said this, an argument arose between the Pharisees and Sadducees, and the crowd was divided.
primaryText.ACT:23:8: For the Sadducees say that there is no resurrection, nor angel, nor spirit; but the Pharisees confess all of these.
primaryText.ACT:23:9: A great clamor arose, and some of the scribes of the Pharisees’ part stood up, and contended, saying, “We find no evil in this man. But if a spirit or angel has spoken to him, let’s not fight against God!”
